findings.description: `GET /api%2fexec%3fcmd=id` is 200 with exactly one `?` upstream, 3/3 cold, exec runs. With `location /apiZ/exec` and `/apiZ%2fexec%3fcmd=id` the decoded `?` falls before the `min()` cut and is dropped, leaving `GET /apiZ%2fexec%20?cmd=id` — exec target present but no `exec` path token and only `query` carrying the command. Two decoded `?` survive as `GET /apiZ%2fexec%20?a?cmd=id` (two `?` on the line), which any first-`?`-only parser mis-splits.
findings.title: Same guard-versus-sink split, plus a lossy `min()` splice that drops a decoded `?` before the cut and passes two `?` through

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
